// Suppressing a borrowed checker with "this closure declares that name
// somewhere" is wrong in both directions. Go's scope for a short variable
// declaration begins at the end of the declaration, so an assertion written
// above it still runs on the parent's checker; and a name an enclosing block
// bound to something that is not a checker at all does not become one by being
// spelled c.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

func TestDeclarationAfterTheUse(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(1, qt.Equals, 1)

	t.Run("the assertion above the declaration is the parent's", func(t *testing.T) {
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)

		c := qt.New(t)
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})
}

func TestDeclarationInsideANestedBlock(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(4, qt.Equals, 4)

	t.Run("a nested block never covers the closure's own", func(t *testing.T) {
		c.Assert(5, qt.Equals, 5)

		{
			c := qt.New(t)
			c.Assert(6, qt.Equals, 6)
		}
	})
}

// An enclosing block takes the name over for something that is not a checker,
// so the closure reads an int and nothing crosses the boundary.
func TestUnrelatedShadowIsNotABorrowedChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(7, qt.Equals, 7)

	{
		c := 8

		t.Run("the c this closure reads is an int", func(t *testing.T) {
			inner := qt.New(t)
			inner.Assert(c, qt.Equals, 8)
		})
	}
}
